title: Reason or Recite: Complementary Specialists with an LLM Judge for Traffic Anomaly Reasoning

body: Road anomalies such as collisions, violations, and sudden hazards demand more from video understanding than detection: a practical system must verify what happened, describe the scene, and explain the cause. We find these competences pull in opposite directions for vision-language models: closed-form questions reward precise, evidence-grounded reasoning, while open-ended answers are scored by similarity to reference text, where matching the annotation style matters as much as reasoning correctly. We present Reason-or-Recite (RoR), a two-specialist framework for the Traffic Anomaly Reasoning track of the 2026 AI City Challenge. RoR (1) rewrites the official chain-of-thought annotations into a structured, temporally grounded schema and LoRA-tunes a 9B vision-language model on the enhanced traces; (2) fine-tunes a 4-bit-quantized 27B model on answers alone, absorbing the annotation style; and (3) selects between the two candidates per question with a training-free LLM judge. RoR ranks first on the in-domain leaderboard with mean score 0.6788.
summaryZh: 推理或背诵：与法学硕士法官一起进行交通异常推理的补充专家。碰撞、违规和突发危险等道路异常对视频理解的要求比检测更多：实用的系统必须验证发生的情况、描述场景并解释原因。我们发现这些能力对视觉语言模型产生相反的影响：封闭式问题奖励精确的、基于证据的推理，而开放式答案则根据与参考文本的相似性进行评分，其中匹配注释风格与正确推理一样重要。
